paper.title: Accurate prediction of tensorial spectra using equivariant graph neural network
paper.research_summary: This paper introduces the Tensorial Spectra Equivariant Neural Network (TSENN), an equivariant graph neural network that maps crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors—specifically, the complex dielectric tensor εαβ(ω) = εαβ₁(ω) + iεαβ₂—trained on frequency-dependent dielectric tensors of 1,432 bulk semiconductors. The model encodes isotropic (ℓ=0) and anisotropic (ℓ=2) sequential tensor components into spherical tensor representations to ensure symmetry-aware predictions consistent with crystalline symmetry constraints, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.127.

task.objective: Map crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors
output_goal: complex dielectric tensor εαβ(ω) = εαβ₁(ω) + iεαβ₂

evidence.text: Here we introduce the Tensorial Spectra Equivariant Neural Network (TSENN), an equivariant graph neural network architecture that maps crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors.

By encoding isotropic sequential scalar components and anisotropic sequential tensor components into spherical tensor representations, TSENN ensures symmetry-aware predictions consistent with crystalline symmetry constraints.

Trained on frequency-dependent dielectric tensors of 1,432 bulk semiconductors, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.127, demonstrating its potential for efﬁcient and general modeling of optical properties.

stages.stage_name_raw: ab initio calculation of dielectric tensors
stages.stage_goal: Compute frequency-dependent dielectric tensors for 1432 nonmagnetic semiconductors using first-principles methods

evidence.text: By training TSENN on the aforementioned dataset, we achieve a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.127 in the predicted imaginary part of the dielectric tensor.

We demonstrate the capabilities of TSENN by considering the frequency-dependent dielectric tensors of a dataset of 1432 nonmagnetic semiconductors calculated via ﬁrst-principles methods using OpenMX37–40.

The dielectric tensors were computed using the Kubo formula for photon energies ranging from 0 to 30 eV, with an increment of 0.01 eV, resulting in 1432 frequency-dependent dielectric tensors satisfying the symmetry constraints of the crystal systems considered45–47.

stages.stage_goal: Transform Cartesian dielectric tensors into spherical-harmonics basis to encode rotational symmetry

evidence.text: To predict the dielectric tensor using an equivariant neural network, we express it in the spherical-harmonics basis, which naturally encodes rotational symmetry.

Since we are dealing with frequency-dependent tensors, we take the Cartesian tensor at each photon energy, perform this change-of-basis operation, and obtain the frequency-dependent spherical-harmonic coefficients as our target, as shown in Fig. 2.

stages.stage_goal: Train equivariant graph neural network to predict spherical-harmonic coefficients from crystal graphs

evidence.text: After the final pointwise convolution layer, we apply mean pooling over all nodes to obtain a global representation of the material. The network output is then partitioned into two parts: a scalar component corresponding to ℓ= 0 and a tensor component corresponding to ℓ= 2.
To train the model, we define a composite loss function L, which separately evaluates the scalar and tensor components of the predicted optical spectra.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluation of dielectric tensor prediction accuracy
stages.stage_goal: Quantify prediction accuracy using MAE and other metrics on full-tensor and per-component levels

evidence.text: To evaluate the model’s performance, the most direct measure is the MAE of the dielectric tensor, MAE = 1/(6nω) Σ_ω Σ_{α≤β} |bε_αβ(ω) − ε_αβ(ω)|.

Table 1 summarizes error metrics for dielectric tensor predictions across chemically and structurally diverse test systems. The overall tensor MAE is 0.127 (0.097 median), establishing TSENN’s robust baseline accuracy.

stages.stage_name_raw: reconstruction of real dielectric part via Kramers–Kronig relations
stages.stage_goal: Validate internal consistency of predicted spectra by reconstructing real part from predicted imaginary part
stage_input: predicted imaginary part of dielectric tensor
stage_output: reconstructed real part of dielectric tensor

evidence.text: With the accurately predicted imaginary parts, we used K–K relations to obtain the real parts of the dielectric tensors.
In Fig. 4b, we compare the real parts obtained via K–K relations from the predicted imaginary spectra against the reference real parts computed directly using the Kubo formula.

stages.stage_goal: Verify model preserves crystalline symmetry by comparing predicted vs. target tensors across symmetry classes

evidence.text: To further confirm symmetry preservation, we applied a symmetry-based masking procedure to the predicted tensor at each photon energy (see Methods).

In the Cartesian tensor representation, the predicted dielectric tensor exhibits symmetry-consistent behavior, correctly reproducing the expected nonzero tensor components in agreement with the ground truth.
